Core Concept · JSON

What Is JSON?

JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is a lightweight, easy-to-read data interchange format. Data is stored as key-value pairs — the native format of JavaScript and the default export format of Firebase.

FORMAT

Key-Value Pairs

Every field is a named key mapped to a typed value — string, number, boolean, array, or nested object.

USAGE

Universal Web Standard

Transmits data between servers and clients. Natively supported by every modern browser, JavaScript runtime, and Firebase.

JSON
{
  "name": "Maria Santos",
  "age": 20,
  "id": "2024-001-IT",
  "location": "Cebu City",
  "course": "BS Information Technology"
}
Firebase Console — Welcome Screen
Hands-On · Firebase Setup

Creating a Firebase Project

  1. Sign In to Firebase ConsoleGo to console.firebase.google.com and sign in with your Google account. Click "Get started by setting up a Firebase project."
  2. Name Your ProjectEnter a project name (e.g., FirstProject). Firebase generates a unique project ID like firstproject-a2a18. Accept the Firebase terms and click Continue.
  3. Configure Google AnalyticsSelect your country/region, accept the Google Analytics terms, and click "Create project." Wait for provisioning to finish, then click Continue.
Step 2 — Naming your project
Step 3 — Google Analytics setup
Hands-On · Navigate to Realtime DB

Finding the Realtime Database

Once your project is created, navigate to the Realtime Database product inside the Firebase Console.

  1. Open Your Project DashboardAfter project creation, you land on the Project Overview page. Look at the left sidebar under Product categories.
  2. Expand "Databases & Storage"Click to reveal options. Under the NoSQL category, you'll see both Firestore and Realtime Database.
  3. Select "Realtime Database"Click it to land on the Realtime Database product page where you can provision your database instance.
Project dashboard — Databases & Storage menu expanded
Hands-On · Database Configuration

Setting Up the Realtime Database

  1. Click "Create Database"On the Realtime Database landing page, click the Create Database button to start the setup wizard.
  2. Choose Your LocationA dialog appears. Choose the server region closest to you. For Southeast Asia, select Singapore (asia-southeast1). Click Next.
  3. Select "Start in test mode"This opens read/write access for 30 days — ideal for learning. Click Enable to confirm and provision your database.
Step 5 — Location: Singapore (asia-southeast1)
Step 6 — Security rules: test mode selected
Security Checkpoint

Test Mode vs. Locked Mode

When creating a database for learning, it's important to understand what security mode you're activating.

✓ Test Mode

  • Data is open by default for quick setup
  • Anyone with your database URL can read/write/delete
  • Access expires automatically after 30 days
  • Best for: learning, prototypes, classroom labs

🔒 Locked Mode

  • Data is private by default — nothing is accessible
  • Access only granted by custom security rules you write
  • No automatic expiry — fully manual configuration
  • Best for: production apps with real users
JSON
{
  "rules": {
    ".read": "now < 1787414400000",   // 2026-8-23
    ".write": "now < 1787414400000"   // 2026-8-23
  }
}
⚠ Warning: Test mode gives anyone with your URL full access to your data. Always update your security rules before deploying any real application.
Hands-On · Adding Data

Your Database Is Live — Now Add Data

After enabling, the database shows null (empty). Click the + icon beside your database URL to add key-value pairs.

  1. Click the + IconClick the + button on the right side of the database URL to open the key-value entry form.
  2. Enter Key & ValueAdd fields one at a time. Example: Key = Name, Value = "Someone". Repeat for each field, then click Add.
  3. Verify in the TreeYour data appears in the JSON tree immediately — synced to the cloud in real time. The database URL now shows your populated records.

Address"Cabatuan"
Age22

Core Concept · cURL

What Is cURL?

cURL (Client URL) is a command-line tool and library for transferring data using URLs. It supports HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and many other protocols — making it a universal tool for interacting with web APIs like Firebase directly from your terminal.

HTTP METHODS

GET, POST, PUT, DELETE

cURL can perform all standard HTTP operations — fetch data, send data, update records, and delete them.

VERSATILE

Scripting & API Testing

Widely used for data retrieval, form submission, API testing, and automation in development pipelines.

BUILT-IN

Pre-installed on Windows 10+

Modern Windows, macOS, and Linux include cURL by default. Verify with curl --version.

CLIENT ↔ cURL/REST ↔ FIREBASE API ↔ REALTIME DATABASE — live JSON cycle
Hands-On · cURL Walkthrough

Retrieving Firebase Data via CLI

Open Command Prompt (Windows) and follow these steps to fetch your Realtime Database content as JSON.

  1. Open Command PromptPress Win + R, type cmd, press Enter.
  2. Navigate to System32Type cd\ → cd windows → cd system
  3. Verify cURL Is AvailableType curl --help — if you see the options list, cURL is installed and ready.
  4. Fetch Firebase DataRun the curl command with your database URL plus .json appended at the end (see next slide).
BASH
C:\Users\Aoi>curl --help
Usage: curl [options...] <url>
 -d, --data <data>           HTTP POST data
 -f, --fail                  Fail fast with no output on HTTP errors
 -h, --help <subject>        Get help for commands
 -o, --output <file>         Write to file instead of stdout
 -O, --remote-name           Write output to file named as remote file
 -i, --show-headers          Show response headers in output
 -s, --silent                Silent mode
 -T, --upload-file <file>    Transfer local FILE to destination
 -u, --user <user:password>  Server user and password
 -v, --verbose               Make the operation more talkative
 -V, --version               Show version number and quit
Live Demo · cURL Output

The JSON Response

Append .json to your Firebase database URL and cURL returns all stored data as a JSON string. This is what a real successful response looks like.

BASH
# Rule: ALWAYS add .json to the end of your Firebase URL
# Without .json  ->  Firebase returns nothing
# With .json     ->  Firebase returns your data as JSON

C:\Users\Aoi>curl "https://firstproject-a2a18-default-rtdb.asia-southeast1.firebasedatabase.app/.json"

{"Address":"Cabatuan","Age":22,"Name":"Someone","Occupation":"Tanod"}
✓ SUCCESS

What You Just Did

Made a GET request to the Firebase REST API and received a live JSON payload — no app code required, just one command.

⇧ EXPORT

Alternative: Console Export

In the Firebase Console, click the ⋮ (three-dot menu) beside your database URL and select "Export JSON" to download a file.

Core Concept · NoSQL

What Is NoSQL?

NoSQL — short for "Not Only SQL" — describes a family of databases designed as an alternative to traditional relational (SQL) databases. They handle large volumes of unstructured or semi-structured data with greater flexibility and scalability.

DEFINITION

NoSQL databases are designed to handle large volumes of unstructured or semi-structured data and provide greater flexibility and scalability than SQL databases for use cases such as real-time apps, big data pipelines, content management systems, and distributed cloud environments.

FLEXIBLE

No Fixed Schema

Add or change fields without altering an entire table. Each record can have a unique structure.

SCALABLE

Horizontal Scaling

Distribute data across many servers easily — ideal for apps handling millions of simultaneous users.

FAST

Optimized for Use-Cases

Each type is built for specific access patterns — blazing fast reads/writes in the scenarios they target.

Core Concept · NoSQL Types

Four Types of NoSQL Databases

📄

Document Databases

Store data as flexible documents (JSON, BSON, XML). Structure can differ between records. Ideal for content management, e-commerce, and mobile apps.

MongoDB · CouchDB · Couchbase · MarkLogic
🔗

Graph Databases

Organize data as nodes (entities) and edges (relationships). Built to map complex interconnected data like social networks or recommendation engines.

Neo4j · AllegroGraph · IBM Graph
🔑

Key-Value Stores

Pair each unique key with a single value using a simple data model. Extremely fast and scalable. Perfect for caching, session management, and shopping carts.

Redis · DynamoDB · Aerospike · Riak
📊

Wide-Column Stores

Tables where column names and formatting can differ row-by-row. Each column stored separately on disk — optimized for querying by column. Used in fraud detection and analytics.

Cassandra · HBase · Amazon SimpleDB
Core Concept · Trade-Offs

Advantages & Disadvantages of NoSQL

✓ Advantages

  • Simplifies development for real-time web apps using REST APIs
  • Flexible data models — no schema migrations for new fields
  • High scalability for large datasets in analytics and AI applications
  • Well-suited for cloud, mobile, social media, and big data
  • Optimized for specific use cases — faster than SQL in those scenarios

✗ Disadvantages

  • No universal query language — each system uses its own syntax
  • Lack of rigid schema removes built-in data integrity safeguards
  • Schema consistency must be enforced by the developer, not the DB
  • Eventual consistency model — unsuitable for banking/ATM-level transactions
  • Newer technology — fewer comprehensive industry-wide standards
FIREBASE NOTE

The Firebase Realtime Database is a NoSQL database that stores your entire dataset as a single large JSON tree — fast, flexible, and ideal for real-time client synchronization.

C. Lesson Wrap-Up · FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

What is NoSQL and why is it used?

NoSQL (Not Only SQL) databases use various data models — document, graph, key-value, wide-column — and are specifically optimized for applications requiring large data volumes, low latency, and flexible data structures. They achieve this by relaxing some of the strict consistency rules enforced by relational databases.

What is the difference between CMD and CLI?

CLI (Command Line Interface) is the general concept of any text-based interface for interacting with an operating system or application. CMD (Command Prompt) is Microsoft's specific Windows implementation of that concept — equivalent to the Terminal (Bash/Zsh) on macOS and Linux.

Why must I add .json to the Firebase URL in cURL?

Firebase's Realtime Database communicates through a REST API. Appending .json tells the Firebase server to respond in JSON format. Without it, Firebase does not know which format you are requesting and returns nothing.

Answers Revealed

Answer Key — Complete Explanations

Multiple Choice (Q1–Q6)

  • Q1 → A. JavaScript Object Notation — JSON is the full name.
  • Q2 → C. .json — required by Firebase REST API to return data.
  • Q3 → D. Graph Database — uses nodes and edges for relationships.
  • Q4 → C. Key-Value Stores — Redis, DynamoDB, Aerospike are examples.
  • Q5 → D. Test Mode — allows open access for 30 days; ideal for learning.
  • Q6 → C. No universal query syntax — unlike SQL which is a universal standard.

Identification (Q1–Q5)

  • 1. JSON — JavaScript Object Notation.
  • 2. Graph Databases — nodes + edges model relationships.
  • 3. cURL — CLI tool for HTTP requests to APIs.
  • 4. Wide-Column Stores — variable columns per row, disk-level column storage.
  • 5. NoSQL — Not Only SQL; the non-relational database family.
